source_text:
So, I am wondering if, while these guys work out the technical details, could we start to think about how to teach this material to humans?  ChatGPT came up with a kind of simple Lakatosian style schema, I'm not saying I would adhere to this exactly.

A [Codex] produces a result.
B [Lean] verifies it.
C develops the conceptual interpretation.
D simplifies it.
E writes the textbook account from which everybody subsequently “understands” it.

But approximately on this level, "C" or "D" would correspond to what I was trying to do with the mathematical patterns and the transfer to Zai, which wasn't ever quite as successful as I would have liked it to be, but which still, I think, has some validity even if it still need to sort out some of the details.  My big inspiration came from the fact that Zai 5.2 would correct itself when it made mistakes, which made me think that we could preempt those self-corrections in a strategic way by seeding in memories that would act like rewrite rules.  Then I thought we could seed in even better techniques that came from Codex.  I'd still like to explore all of that, but the ultimate goal was to develop a system that would teach the material to me, or other humans, not Zai.  For that, I thought a good strategy would be to use a pattern cascade, much as I am developing in M-象-2000, but now, for mathematics rather than for general programming.  I figure if we could develop a few such treatments, that would serve as a proof of principle, because I have forgotten almost all of this material (if I ever knew much of it, which is a bit doubtful).  Something else to say here is that we did translate the informal solutions to LaTeX for further processing via the futon6 superpod markup routines, but that is waiting on a suitable moment.  The superpod would be great for helping with "conceptual interpretation" and that doesn't even rely on the Lean code at all!
